confirmed: The entire local markdown was read, including references and Appendix A (lines 1-394). The corresponding PDF has nine pages; PDF p. 1 identifies arXiv:2311.01937v1, dated 3 Nov 2023, titled Supermind Ideator: Exploring generative AI to support creative problem-solving, with Steven R. Rick and Gianni Giacomelli first. This supports the source.version distinction from the target journal article.

The local earlier PDF reports a formative study with 40 participants, who were professionals; this is a count of people, not ideas or ratings (PDF p. 5, section 5, Evaluation). It gives no separate randomized and analyzed counts. This sample is below 50 but must not be substituted for the target experiment.

The earlier study used remote think-aloud sessions and collected user-experience insights and professional applicability feedback, with no reported random allocation to AI conditions or scored participant-output creativity/diversity comparison (local PDF p. 5, section 5). Quantitative evaluation of idea quality is described as underway (PDF p. 6, section 7), and Appendix A contains API instructions (PDF p. 9).

The target title and author list match the Crossref journal record for DOI 10.1177/26339137241305117; its abstract explicitly compares people using Supermind Ideator, people using ChatGPT, and people working alone (https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1177/26339137241305117, title, author, and abstract fields; read 2026-10-09).

The target abstract supplies no assignment mechanism, participant counts, exclusions, scoring method, numerical effect estimate, test statistic, confidence interval, or exact p value. The form correctly leaves these quantities unconfirmed and does not transfer the earlier study sample (target Crossref abstract, entire text).

The existing reported statement about significantly greater innovativeness than ChatGPT is supported, and the one_line_finding correctly includes the working-alone comparison. Neither claims a numerical effect absent from the abstract (target Crossref abstract, results sentence).

The accessible target evidence describes human AI assistance rather than standalone AI versus human output, an observational comparison, or a synthesis. design_class other, assignment.randomized not_stated, and context_class none appropriately preserve the unresolved design; no synthesis study count or pooled estimate is supported (target Crossref abstract, entire text).

has_randomized_people_study=false means that no such study could be verified from the sources read, not that its absence from the target full text has been established. The target remains unresolved for full-text screening because the abstract calls it experimental without specifying randomization (target Crossref abstract, results sentence).

Independent retrieval confirmed access failures for the target and erratum SAGE full-text pages (HTTP 403), the ACM conference PDF (HTTP 403), and the MIT repository conference PDF (HTTP 405). Crossref confirms an erratum at DOI 10.1177/26339137251409515 but provides no abstract; its content and any corrections to results remain unverified (https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1177/26339137251409515, title, abstract, and update-to fields; read 2026-10-09).
summary: The form correctly distinguishes the earlier 40-person usability study from the target experiment, whose randomization and participant counts remain unverified. Core eligibility should remain unclear, both abstract-supported contrasts and AI availability should be recorded, and company involvement should remain unknown.
